paper_metadata.title: Room temperature fracture toughness and high temperature strength of T2/Moss and (Mo,Nb)ss/T1/T2 eutectic alloys in the Mo–Si–B system

evidence.quote: Multiphase Mo–Si–B alloys are potential candidates for ultra-high temperature application.
The eutectic alloys investigated have three different compositions: Mo–9Si–18B, ... (at.%).
The eutectic alloys investigated have three different compositions: Mo–9Si–18B, ... (at.%).
The eutectic alloys investigated have three different compositions: Mo–9Si–18B, ... (at.%).
The eutectic alloys investigated have three different compositions: Mo–9Si–18B, (Mo0.6Nb0.4)–19.5Si–4.5B (Mo–30.4Nb–19.5Si–4.5B) and (Mo0.5Nb0.5)–19.5Si–3B (Mo–38.75Nb–19.5Si–3B) (at.%).

other.feedstock: high-purity Mo, Nb, Si and B

evidence.quote: Rods, 10 mm in diameter and 80 mm in length, were prepared by Ar arc-melting of high-purity Mo, Nb, Si and B.
Directionally solidified specimens were grown from the rods using our ASGAL FZ-SS35W optical floating-zone (FZ) furnace at a growth rate of 2.5–200 mm/h under an Ar gas flow.

evidence.quote: Rods, 10 mm in diameter and 80 mm in length, were prepared by Ar arc-melting of high-purity Mo, Nb, Si and B.

Fig. 1 shows SEM micrographs of eutectic microstructures of (a), (b) Mo–9Si–18B, (c), (d) (Mo0.6Nb0.4)–19.5Si–4.5B and (e), (f) (Mo0.5Nb0.5)–19.5Si–3B alloys, respectively, directionally solidified at growth rates of 5, 2.5 and 200 mm/h.

evidence.section: 3.2. High temperature strength and fracture toughness at room temperature
evidence.quote: The (Mo0.5Nb0.5)–19.5Si–3B alloy has a 0.2% proof stress at 1500 °C of about 400 MPa. There is no significant difference in the 0.2% proof stress at high temperatures between (Mo0.5Nb0.5)–19.5Si–3B alloys directionally solidified at growth rates of 10 and 200 mm/h.
Directionally solidified specimens were grown from the rods using our ASGAL FZ-SS35W optical floating-zone (FZ) furnace at a growth rate of 2.5–200 mm/h under an Ar gas flow.
The volume fraction of Moss is estimated to be about 28 vol.% on the basis of the phase diagram.

evidence.section: 3.2. High temperature strength and fracture toughness at room temperature
evidence.quote: Many obvious microcracks are observed in a T2 matrix of the two-phase Mo–9Si–18B alloy deformed at 1500 °C
The Mo–9Si–18B alloy has a T2/Moss two-phase eutectic microstructure, which can be obtained at a growth rate of less than 5 mm/h.
The two alloys in the (Mo,Nb)–Si–B system have a (Mo,Nb)ss/T1/T2 three-phase eutectic microstructure (Fig. 1(c)–(f)).
The two alloys in the (Mo,Nb)–Si–B system have a (Mo,Nb)ss/T1/T2 three-phase eutectic microstructure (Fig. 1(c)–(f)).

attributes.phase_fraction: lower volume fraction than (Mo,Nb)_ss and T1

evidence.quote: The two alloys in the (Mo,Nb)–Si–B system have a (Mo,Nb)ss/T1/T2 three-phase eutectic microstructure (Fig. 1(c)–(f)).
In both (Mo,Nb)–Si–B alloys, the (Mo,Nb)ss and T1 have similar volume fraction. The T2 has a lower volume fraction either of the other two phases.

attributes.morphology: degenerate or discontinuous eutectic lamellar structure

evidence.quote: It resembles a degenerate or discontinuous eutectic lamellar structure and can be obtained in a substitution of Mo atoms by about 30 at.% Nb atoms.
The Mo atoms were substituted by about 61, 58 and 32 at.% Nb atoms in the T1, T2 and bcc phases of the (Mo0.5Nb0.5)–19.5Si–3B alloy, respectively.
The Mo atoms were substituted by about 61, 58 and 32 at.% Nb atoms in the T1, T2 and bcc phases of the (Mo0.5Nb0.5)–19.5Si–3B alloy, respectively.
The Mo atoms were substituted by about 61, 58 and 32 at.% Nb atoms in the T1, T2 and bcc phases of the (Mo0.5Nb0.5)–19.5Si–3B alloy, respectively.
The three-phase eutectic microstructure is refined with increasing growth rate, resulting in a sub-micron eutectic microstructure at a growth rate of 200 mm/h (Fig. 1(f)).

evidence.section: 3.2. High temperature strength and fracture toughness at room temperature
evidence.quote: This is consistent with crack deflection along the T2/Moss interface in the Mo–9Si–18B specimen, so that when the length of the Moss short rods is parallel to direction of crack propagation, crack has proceeded along the Moss/T2 interface, and the Moss rod has been pulled out.

evidence.section: 3.2. High temperature strength and fracture toughness at room temperature
evidence.quote: For the (Mo,Nb)ss/T1/T2 three-phase alloy, its macrodeformation appears to have a solid solution phase effect similar to the two-phase Mo–9Si–18B alloy at 1200 °C.

mechanisms.name: catastrophic failure avoidance by Mo_ss addition

evidence.section: 3.2. High temperature strength and fracture toughness at room temperature
evidence.quote: The macrodeformation of Mo–9Si–18B alloys occurs through cracking of the T2 matrix and plastic deformation of the Moss and therefore the catastrophic failure of the monolithic T2 can be avoided by addition of the second phase Moss to the T2 matrix.
